sources.title: Rust macros by example expanding to patterns
sources.version_or_date: Live Rust Reference, no publication date established
sources.sections_read: Macro definition and expansion contexts; fragment capture and forwarding; Hygiene via find.
sources.confirmed: The reference permits macros to produce patterns as well as expressions and explains typed fragment capture. Its hygiene rules require attention to which identifiers originate at definition and invocation sites.
sources.limits: This is current documentation, not evidence that pattern expansion was available at the 2014 cutoff; identifier hygiene, fragment opacity, and permitted follow tokens constrain composition. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C19.json.

sources.title: Whole-match expression macros, illustrated by Rust matches!
sources.version_or_date: Live main branch; matches! annotation since 1.42.0
sources.sections_read: Public source file; matches! declaration and generated match expression located with find; adjacent try! implementation.
sources.confirmed: The actual core source defines matches! by capturing an expression, a pattern, and an optional guard, then emitting a complete match expression. Its stability annotation names Rust 1.42.0; the separately opened 2020 release announcement confirms when that standard macro stabilized.
sources.limits: The observed matches! implementation returns only a Boolean and does not export bindings; carrying parsed components or preserving arm layout needs a custom wrapper, and this example is later evidence. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C19.json.

sources.title: GHC parameterized pattern synonyms
sources.sections_read: Line-specific open at 120: pattern guards, view-pattern semantics and optimization limits, opening of pattern-synonym section.
sources.confirmed: View patterns apply a function to the matched value and match its result, allowing representation-specific deconstruction to live behind a reusable function. The guide also describes limited sharing of repeated view calls.
sources.limits: This is a Haskell mechanism to adapt to Rust, not a Rust library; binding, typing, ownership, and whether construction is supported need explicit design. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C19.json.

sources.title: Racket define-match-expander
sources.sections_read: Archived Pattern Matching page; section 8.2 Extending match located with find.
sources.confirmed: The archived Racket 5.3 documentation defines a named pattern transformer and an optional expression transformer and illustrates a reusable syntax-list matcher. The official release index dates this documentation version to August 2012.
sources.limits: The mechanism belongs to Racket's syntax and match library; a Rust transfer must define recognition, binding hygiene, diagnostics, and the valid output pattern category. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C19.json.

sources.title: Scala extractor objects using unapply
sources.version_or_date: Archived Scala 2.11 specification; dated change entry for 2.3.2 (2007-01-23)
sources.sections_read: Changelog opening; Changes in Version 2.3.2 / Extractors located with find.
sources.confirmed: The official changelog dates the extractor change to January 23, 2007 and explains how unapply returns an optional tuple of pattern bindings. This dated historical entry supports pre-cutoff availability of the mechanism.
sources.limits: Scala's constructor-like extractor syntax is not provided by the cited Rust mechanism; an ordinary Rust helper changes how matches are written, and effectful extractors or opaque failure can complicate reasoning. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C19.json.

sources.sections_read: Line-specific open at 193: parameterized pattern synonyms, representation abstraction, unidirectional and bidirectional forms.
sources.confirmed: Pattern synonyms give reusable names to nested pattern structures while retaining constructor-like matching syntax. Unidirectional forms can hide structure that cannot be reconstructed uniquely, whereas bidirectional forms can also construct values.
